mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases over a year.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment below 4% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Unemployment falls below 4% but S&P 500 returns are negative in over 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate alongside increasing inflation (CPI) leads to higher borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Both FEDFUNDS and CPI rise, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary easing cycle, lower federal funds rates reduce borrowing costs, stimulating investment and increasing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS are low but S&P 500 returns are negative in over 40% of cases during easing.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production indicates strong economic output, leading to higher S&P 500 returns as supply meets demand.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate exceeds 5%, higher borrowing costs may reduce corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS above 5% but S&P 500 returns positive in over 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment alongside low unemployment indicates a strong economy, boosting S&P 500 returns through increased consumer and business activity.
failure_condition: Employment rises and unemployment falls, but S&P 500 returns are negative in over 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing expansion regime, increased housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns through related industries.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.
